The Fortis Memorial Research Institute (FMRI) in [[Gurgaon]] serves as the headquarters for Fortis Healthcare.{{Cite web |title=Fortis Memorial Research Institute bags recognition as smart hospital |url=https://www.biospectrumindia.com/news/16/18848/fortis-memorial-research-institute-bags-recognition-as-smart-hospital.html |access-date=2022-03-16 |website=www.biospectrumindia.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Newsweek |date=2022-03-02 |title=World's Best Hospitals 2022 - India |url=https://www.newsweek.com/worlds-best-hospitals-2022/india |access-date=2022-03-16 |website=Newsweek |language=en}} In addition to its Gurgaon facility, Fortis Healthcare operates hospitals in the [[Delhi]] [[National Capital Region (India)|NCR]], including locations in [[Faridabad]], [[Noida]], [[Vasant Kunj]], and [[Shalimar Bagh (Delhi)|Shalimar Bagh]], along with other facilities across India, [[Dubai]], and [[Sri Lanka]]. The company currently{{when|date=May 2025}} manages 36 healthcare facilities.{{Cite web|url=https://www.fortishealthcare.com/about-us|title=Fortis Healthcare – About Us}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.zaubacorp.com/company/FORTIS-HEALTHCARE-LIMITED/L85110PB1996PLC045933|title=FORTIS HEALTHCARE LIMITED - Company, directors and contact details | Zauba Corp}} == History == Fortis Healthcare was founded in 1996 as an offshoot of the pharmaceutical company [[Ranbaxy Laboratories]].{{cite news |last1= Gupta |first1=Ashish |last2=Ghosh| first2=Debojyoti |title=The war for Fortis |url=https://www.fortuneindia.com/enterprise/the-war-for-fortis/101995 |access-date=8 May 2025 |work=Fortune India |date=13 June 2018 |language=en}} It began operating in [[Mohali]], [[Punjab, India|Punjab]], where its first hospital was established. It later expanded by acquiring the healthcare division of [[Escorts Group]], including the Escorts Heart and Research Center, [[Okhla]], [[Delhi]].{{cite news |title=Fortis acquires Escorts Heart |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/fortis-acquires-escorts-heart-105092901002_1.html |access-date=8 May 2025 |work=Business Standard |date=29 September 2005}} In February 2018, founders [[Malvinder Mohan Singh|Malvinder Singh]] and [[Shivinder Mohan Singh|Shivinder Singh]] resigned from the board of Fortis Healthcare following allegations that they had siphoned $78 million out of the company. A month earlier, the [[Delhi High Court]] had upheld a 2016 Singapore arbitration tribunal order against the Singh brothers to pay {{INR}}3,500 crore ($550 million) in damages to [[Daiichi Sankyo]] for misrepresenting information during the sale of [[Ranbaxy Laboratories]].{{cite news |last1=Altstedter |first1=Ari |last2=Smith Alexander |first2=George |last3=P R |first3=Sanjai |title=Singhs Said to Have Taken $78 Million From Fortis Healthcare |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-02-09/indian-tycoons-are-said-to-have-taken-78-million-out-of-fortis |access-date=8 May 2025 |work=Bloomberg |date=9 February 2018}}{{cite news |last1=Thacker |first1=Teena |title=Fortis Healthcare promoters Malvinder, Shivinder Singh resign from board |url=https://www.livemint.com/Companies/rwRFmyh5Dlc8CQscZNg4RM/Fortis-Healthcare-promoters-Malvinder-Shivinder-Singh-resig.html |access-date=8 May 2025 |work=Mint |date=8 February 2018}} In March 2018, [[Manipal Hospitals]] and [[TPG Capital]] offered to buy out Singh brothers' stake in Fortis Healthcare for {{INR}}3,900 crore.{{cite news |title=Fortis Healthcare Ltd. |url=https://www.business-standard.com/company/fortis-health-24049/information/company-history |newspaper=Business Standard India}}{{cite web |last1=Sen |first1=Amiti |title=Manipal Hospitals buys Fortis hospitals biz |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/manipal-hospitals-buys-fortis-hospitals-biz/article23370334.ece |website=@businessline |date=28 March 2018 |language=en}}{{cite news |title=TPG-backed Manipal acquires Fortis Health, SRL Diagnostics |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/tpg-backed-manipal-acquires-fortis-health-srl-diagnostics/articleshow/63495248.cms |website=The Times of India|date=28 March 2018 }} After a bidding war,{{cite news |title=Timeline: Fortis Healthcare bidding war - The story so far |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/world/timeline-fortis-healthcare-bidding-war-the-story-so-far-idUSKBN1I2347/ |access-date=8 May 2025 |work=Reuters}} Malaysia's [[IHH Healthcare]] completed the acquisition of a 31.1% controlling stake for {{INR}}4,000 crore. Representatives from IHH Healthcare were appointed to the board of Fortis.{{cite news| url=https://www.livemint.com/Companies/n5hz8EnQh6C9rcD5JvVZYM/IHH-acquires-controlling-311-stake-in-Fortis-for-Rs-4000.html | title=IHH Healthcare completes Fortis deal by acquiring 31% stake | extract:
Fortis Healthcare Limited is an Indian for-profit private hospital network headquartered in Gurgaon. 
The Fortis Memorial Research Institute (FMRI) in Gurgaon serves as the headquarters for Fortis Healthcare. In addition to its Gurgaon facility, Fortis Healthcare operates hospitals in the Delhi NCR, including locations in Faridabad, Noida, Vasant Kunj, and Shalimar Bagh, along with other facilities across India, Dubai, and Sri Lanka. The company currently manages 36 healthcare facilities.
